correctness.rationale: For a first rod at u and L=n-1+epsilon, the sum floor(u)+floor(L-u) equals n-1 exactly when the fractional part of u is at most epsilon (up to zero-probability boundaries). Each successful split therefore lies in a stated window, and both daughters must attain their respective integer capacities. Conditioning and independent renewal give the exact recursion. Scaling the slack by epsilon gives a weight v^(q-1) times the daughter asymptote in an edge window or a smooth strictly positive density factor times two daughter asymptotes in an interior window; q>0 and nonnegative exponents give integrable domination. The resulting positive beta coefficients have exactly the powers in the displayed recurrence. For a fixed tree, if b vertices have two children, the number of unary vertices is n-1-2b, giving cost q(n-1)+(1-2q)b. A full binary tree with b internal nodes can be extended by a chain of n-1-2b unary nodes above its root, realizing every allowed b; this verifies all minimizing and tying cases. An actual change of topology occurs for n>=3; for n=2 the two descriptions select the same unary topology, as the stated exponent and proof imply. At n=3 the two edge integrals and the central integral have the stated coefficients; their relative O(epsilon) errors follow by using F_2(s)=2s^q/(q B(q,q)) times (1+O(s)) uniformly over the window. The separate point values at zero slack in the integral do not affect it.
